title: Tax-free countries: Where you pay no income tax
summary: See which countries charge no personal income tax, what residency really requires, and the costs behind the headline. Explore the list.
body_markdown:
Nothing can beat that feeling of waiting for a text/email alert telling you that your salary has landed, only to finally receive it and see that part of your income is missing because you've had ‘income tax’ taken out.


Income tax is a tax charged by governments on the income earned by individuals. This could be money earned from a salary, wages, business profits, or other personal income. In many countries, income tax will automatically be deducted from your salary as an employee. Self-employed individuals may be required to calculate and pay personal income tax themselves.


Governments use this to fund public services and infrastructure such as healthcare, education, transport, and security.


However, how much is paid, who pays, and how income is taxed will depend on the country. A handful of countries charge no personal income tax, mostly Gulf states, Caribbean islands, and small European territories. They usually raise money through VAT, customs duties, or residency fees instead. Becoming a tax resident takes time and money, and US citizens still file on worldwide income.


There are 12 countries globally where you can legally live and work in 2026 with 100% of your personal income and investment earnings.


While you won’t pay any income tax, you will still have to pay tax in some form. All governments need to pay for their roads, hospitals, and public services. So, instead of charging you tax on your payslip, you will pay tax on your groceries, importing a car, renting a flat, or running a business.


If you are working abroad, working remotely, or considering moving abroad, understanding the differences can help you make smarter financial decisions. Here are 12 countries where you can earn income without paying personal income tax.


## **What does “tax-free” mean?**


When searching for countries with no tax, people often imagine they can earn 100% of their income with no further interaction with a revenue body. However, zero-tax countries rely heavily on indirect and corporate taxes such as


**VAT and sales duties:** Value Added Tax is a consumption tax charged on everyday items and services. Instead of charging tax on the income you earn, you’ll pay tax on the money you spend. Many Gulf states have introduced VAT in the last decade. While you may not pay any tax on your salary in Riyadh or Manama, you’ll pay 15% VAT in Saudi Arabia and 10% VAT in Bahrain.


**Import and customs duties:** Taxes charged on goods imported into a country. It is usually paid by the importer at the border and will therefore increase the price you pay in shops. Many Caribbean and Pacific island economies depend heavily on imported goods, so customs duties, shipping costs and insurance can make everyday items such as food, electronics and vehicles more expensive.


**Corporate and freelance tax:** This is a tax paid on the net profit of a registered business or self-employed individual. Just because a country has no general personal income tax does not mean businesses operating there are excluded from taxation.


As of 2026, the United Arab Emirates charges 9% corporate tax on profits from businesses and freelance work over AED 375,000. Bermuda charges 15% corporate income tax on large multinational groups and progressive payroll tax on local earnings.


**Property and stamp duty:** Stamp duty and property tax are taxes charged by the government, either one-off or annually, on the purchase, sale, or registration of property. If you’re buying or renting property, you’ll pay a high transfer tax, stamp duty, or fees.


Understanding where tax will be charged can help you understand how much it will really cost to live there.


## **Countries with no personal income tax**


There are more than 20 countries and states globally that charge no personal income tax. However, some are difficult to relocate to due to strict visa requirements. Using data from[PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/) and[OECD Automatic Exchange of Information Portal](https://www.oecd.org/en/networks/global-forum-tax-transparency/resources/aeoi-implementation-portal.html) , here are 12 countries with no income tax in 2026. They have been split by region.


### **The Middle East (Gulf Cooperation Council)**


These countries earn enough from oil and gas to fund their roads, schools, and public services without taxing your salary.


#### **1. United Arab Emirates (UAE)**


Dubai and Abu Dhabi are popular destinations for remote workers, business founders, and expats. In 2026, you pay 0% tax on your salary and share dividends and profits from selling personal assets.


You can get a residency visa through a local job, a remote work visa, a freelance permit, or a 10-year Golden Visa by buying property worth at least AED 2 million. On the flip side, you will pay 5% VAT on shopping, a 4% fee when buying property in Dubai and a 9% corporate tax on business profits over AED 375,000.


#### **2. Bahrain**


**‍** Bahrain charges 0% tax on your wages and investment profits. You can move there with a job offer or get a 10-year Golden Residency by buying property worth at least BHD 130,000 or earning BHD 2,000 a month after living there for five years. Everyday costs include a 10% VAT and a 2% property registration fee.


#### **3. Qatar**


**‍** Your salary and personal investment profits are completely tax-free in Qatar.


Property investments of at least QAR 730,000 can qualify eligible foreign buyers for a residence permit without a local sponsor. A higher investment of at least QAR 3.65 million can provide additional permanent-residency-related benefits.


Qatar has no general VAT in force as of November 2026. However, qualifying Qatar-source business income is subject to a 10% income tax. This can include income earned by self-employed individuals carrying out taxable business activities in the country.


#### **4. Saudi Arabia**


**‍** Saudi Arabia charges 0% personal income tax on salaries. Expats usually move there on a work visa or through the Premium Residency programme.


The Premium Residency programme offers different products. These include a renewable one-year residency option costing SAR 100,000 annually and a permanent residency option with a one-time fee of SAR 800,000. Foreign property owners may also qualify for the Real Estate Owner Residency product by owning or holding qualifying rights to residential property worth at least SAR 4 million, subject to the programme’s conditions.


Foreign-owned businesses and qualifying non-Saudi ownership interests in companies may be subject to a 20% corporate income tax on their taxable share of profits. Shoppers pay 15% VAT on most taxable goods and services.


This corporate tax should not be confused with personal income tax on an employee’s salary.


#### **5. Kuwait**


**‍** Kuwait has no personal income tax and no VAT. However, moving there is difficult unless you have a local job offer, family sponsorship, or a licensed local business.


Foreign-owned companies also pay a 15% corporate income tax on profits made in Kuwait.


#### **6. Oman**


**‍** Residents in Oman currently pay 0% general personal income tax. You can move there through an employment arrangement or qualifying property investment and residency programmes.


Oman has introduced legislation on personal income tax from 1 January 2028. Under Royal Decree No. 56/2025, a 5% tax will apply to taxable income above OMR 42,000 annually.


### **The Caribbean and Atlantic**


These island nations pay for public services using tourism, financial services, import taxes, and visa investment fees instead of taxing your salary.


#### **7. The Bahamas**


**‍** The Bahamas charges 0% tax on your salary, investment profits, and inheritance. You can move there on an annual residence permit or get permanent residency by buying property worth at least BSD 750,000.


Since 1 January 2025, the minimum investment for economic permanent residency has been BSD 1 million, maintained for at least 10 years.


Everyday shopping comes with VAT and import duties on many shipped goods. The standard VAT rate is 10%.


However, from 1 April 2026, unprepared food has been made zero-rated for VAT, so the standard rate does not apply to every grocery purchase.


#### **8. Cayman Islands**


**‍** The Cayman Islands charges zero personal income tax, zero tax on investment gains, and zero corporate tax.


It also has no general inheritance or gift tax. However, residents and businesses still face other government charges, including import duties, work permit fees and property stamp duty.


Foreign workers can move there through a local employment arrangement or qualify for certain investment-based residency programmes.


One option is a Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means, which requires an investment of at least US$2 million in developed real estate in the Cayman Islands. Another route, the Certificate of Direct Investment, requires an investment of at least US$1 million in an employment-generating business. Both routes have additional eligibility requirements.


The Global Citizen Concierge Programme is no longer available. It ended in 2022 and should not be considered a current remote-work visa option.


Instead of income tax, the government relies on import duties, financial services licence fees, work permit fees and stamp duties.


#### **9. Bermuda**


**‍** Bermuda does not charge personal income tax or general tax on personal capital gains. However, it does charge payroll tax on employment income.


Employers pay this tax, but they can deduct the employee’s share from their salaries. For the 2026/27 tax year (1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027), employees pay between 0.25% and 12.50%, depending on how much they earn each year. The first BMD 48,000 is taxed at 0.25%, while the highest rate of 12.50% applies to annual earnings between BMD 500,001 and BMD 1 million.


If you want to move to Bermuda, you will need a work permit or another qualifying residency option.


Investors may also qualify through Bermuda’s Economic Investment Residential Certificate (EIRC) programme. The programme requires a minimum investment of BMD 2.5 million in approved areas, such as local property, businesses or certain charitable contributions. Applicants must also meet the programme’s investment, holding and residency requirements.


Bermuda also charges a 15% corporate income tax, but only on qualifying multinational groups with annual global revenues of at least €750 million. This tax does not apply to every business in Bermuda.


#### **10. Antigua and Barbuda**


**‍** Residents of Antigua and Barbuda pay 0% general personal income tax on salaries and personal investment income.


You can explore relocation through the country’s ordinary immigration routes or its Citizenship by Investment Programme, which gives qualifying applicants options such as approved real estate investments and contributions to the National Development Fund. Citizenship is not automatic and is subject to due diligence and other eligibility requirements.


The country’s Nomad Digital Residence programme, which previously allowed remote workers to live there for up to two years, ended on 15 November 2025 and is no longer available to new applicants.


Local companies pay a 25% corporate income tax, while shoppers pay a standard 17% Antigua and Barbuda Sales Tax (ABST) on taxable goods and services.


#### **11. Saint Kitts and Nevis**


**‍** Saint Kitts and Nevis does not charge general personal income tax on employment earnings. Individuals also generally do not pay personal income tax on dividends, interest and capital gains.


Although business income and other specific transactions may be subject to separate tax rules, the absence of personal income tax should not be interpreted as an exemption from every tax obligation.


People from other countries can explore residency or citizenship through qualifying investment routes, including approved real estate purchases or contributions to the Sustainable Island State Contribution.


Applicants must satisfy the programme’s due diligence, financial and other eligibility requirements before citizenship can be granted.


The government generates revenue through a 17% standard VAT, import duties and corporate income tax, which is generally 33% on taxable company profits.


### **Europe**


#### **12. Monaco**


**‍** Monaco charges 0% personal income tax on most residents, except for French nationals who are subject to French income tax under the 1963 agreement between France and Monaco.


To obtain a residence card (carte de séjour), you must demonstrate that you have suitable accommodation in Monaco, provide the required criminal record documentation and show that you have enough financial resources to support yourself.


If you are relying on independent financial means, you can provide a certified statement from a Monaco-based bank with sufficient funds.


You may also qualify through employment, business activity or financial support from another person.


Companies that earn at least 25% of their turnover outside Monaco are subject to corporate profits tax, currently at 25%.


Monaco also applies a standard 20% VAT rate, in line with the French VAT system.

## **How to qualify as a tax resident**


Getting a visa to live in a country doesn’t mean you’ll be a legal tax resident. Most countries have 3 main rules to determine if you’re a tax resident:


**The 183-day rule:** Many countries use the 183-day rule as one of the criteria for determining tax residency, but it is not a universal requirement.


For example, the UAE recognises several routes to tax residency. An individual may qualify after spending at least 183 days in the country within a consecutive 12-month period. There is also a route for individuals who spend between 90 and 182 days in the UAE, provided they meet conditions such as having UAE employment, conducting business there or maintaining a permanent place of residence. A separate route considers whether the UAE is the individual’s primary residence and the centre of their financial and personal interests.


Meeting the requirements for a tax residency certificate is not necessarily the same as meeting the immigration requirements for a residence visa. Always check the rules that apply to your destination and circumstances.


**Money and investment requirements:** If you are not moving for a local job, you may need to show that you can support yourself financially.


Depending on the country and immigration programme, you may have to show proof of remote employment, a minimum monthly income, sufficient savings or qualifying investments.


For example, the Cayman Islands requires at least US$2 million in developed real estate for its Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means. Monaco requires evidence of sufficient financial resources, which can be proven through a certified statement from a local bank. Bermuda’s 2026 Economic Investment Residential Certificate programme requires an investment of at least BMD 2.5 million.


These are separate immigration requirements, not universal tax-residency thresholds. A person can qualify for a residence permit without automatically becoming a tax resident.


**Cutting ties with your home country:**


Moving abroad is only half the job. Your previous country may still consider you a tax resident.


Tax authorities in countries such as the UK, Canada and Australia look at factors including where you maintain your permanent home, where your family lives, your employment arrangements and the location of your economic interests.


Having a bank account, owning property or running a company in your former country does not automatically make you a tax resident there.


Reading up on[how dual citizenship works](https://grey.co/blog/downsides-of-dual-citizenship) or tools like[Estonia e-Residency](https://grey.co/blog/estonia-digital-nomad-visa) can help you understand international legal status, though neither replaces actually moving away to end your home tax obligations.


Visa approvals usually take anywhere from four weeks for a Gulf work permit to six months or more for Caribbean and European investor visas. Make sure to budget for legal fees, health insurance, document checks, and property deposits before you apply.


## **What does it mean for US citizens and other nationals?**


Looking for zero-tax countries for expats works very differently if you hold a US passport because the United States taxes its citizens no matter where they live in the world.


According to the[IRS guide for U.S. citizens and residents abroad](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/us-citizens-and-residents-abroad-filing-requirements) , American citizens and green card holders must file a US tax return and report their worldwide income every year, even if they live full-time in Dubai, Monaco, or the Cayman Islands.


US citizens living abroad may reduce their US tax bill through the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (Form 2555).


For the 2026 tax year, eligible Americans can exclude up to $132,900 of foreign-earned income from US federal income tax. To qualify, they must have a tax home abroad and meet either the physical presence test (spending at least 330 full days outside the US within a 12-month period) or the bona fide residence test (living in another country for an uninterrupted period that includes a full tax year).


The exclusion covers eligible employment and self-employment income, but not dividends, interest or capital gains. Income above the exclusion limit may still be taxable, and rental income follows separate rules.


US citizens abroad may also need to file an FBAR (Foreign Bank Account Report) **if the combined value of their foreign bank and financial accounts exceeds $10,000 at any point during the year.


If you want to reduce your US tax bill without dealing with overseas tax rules, consider moving to a US state with no personal income tax.


Other countries have their own rules for people who stop being tax residents. Canada and South Africa, for example, may tax certain assets as though they were sold when someone leaves. France has an exit tax for some shareholders, while Australia has capital gains tax rules for certain assets. These taxes do not apply to everyone and depend on individual circumstances.


*Note: Breaking international tax rules can lead to heavy fines. This article is not tax advice, so always speak with a qualified cross-border tax advisor about your personal situation.*

## **Frequently asked questions about tax-free countries**


### **Which countries have no income tax?**


12 major countries and territories with zero personal income tax for residents include the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, the Bahamas, the Cayman Islands, Bermuda, Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Kitts and Nevis, and Monaco. Oman has passed legislation to introduce a 5% personal income tax on high earners starting in January 2028.


### **Can Americans avoid tax by moving?**


No. Under IRS rules, US citizens and green card holders are taxed on their worldwide income no matter where they live. While qualifying expats can exclude up to $132,900 of foreign-earned salary in 2026 under the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion, earnings above that threshold and passive investment income remain taxable by the US government.


### **Is Dubai really tax-free?**


Dubai charges 0% personal income tax on salaries, dividends, and personal capital gains. However, residents still pay indirect and business levies, including a 5% Value-Added Tax (VAT) on most goods and services, a 4% property transfer fee, municipal housing fees, and a 9% corporate tax on business or freelance profits above AED 375,000.


### **How long must I stay?**


Most zero-tax jurisdictions require you to spend at least 183 days per year inside the country to qualify as a tax resident and obtain a Tax Residency Certificate. Some destinations, such as the UAE, offer a 90-day residency route if you maintain a permanent residence and strong economic ties locally, while US citizens claiming the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion must spend at least 330 full days abroad.


### **Are there hidden costs?**


Yes. Countries without personal income tax fund public services through higher everyday costs. Expect steeper prices driven by customs duties on imported goods, VAT rates between 5% and 20%, mandatory private health insurance, expensive property minimums, and annual visa or residency renewal fees.


*Disclaimer: This article contains general information only and should not be considered tax advice. Tax laws and residency requirements can change frequently, so always consult a qualified cross-border tax professional.*
